current_episode.title: Brené Brown & Reid Hoffman on the skills every leader needs now

guest.entreprise: University of Houston (Graduate College of Social Work)
guest.bio_context: Brené Brown is an author and researcher who has spent two decades teaching in a graduate college of social work. She has conducted extensive research on courageous leadership, vulnerability, and emotional intelligence, working with C-suite leaders and their direct reports to understand the skills required for effective modern leadership.

pending_qa.q: How should leaders identify and overcome their personal defense mechanisms when facing uncertainty?
pending_qa.r: Leaders should identify their go-to armor—the self-protective behavior they default to when afraid, such as perfectionism, micromanagement, or over-decisiveness. Rather than asking direct reports due to power differentials, leaders should develop their own self-awareness about how they self-protect. If you don't have the insight or courage to think about it, the sanity of leading people should be questioned, because who we are is how we lead.

pending_qa.q: What is the distinction between cognitive empathy and affective empathy in leadership?
pending_qa.r: Cognitive empathy is when someone shares a problem, you reflect back what you hear, and they feel seen, heard, and believed—this is the source code for relationships and democracy. Affective empathy is when you feel what the other person is feeling, which is not helpful and leads to burnout and actually minimizes compassion. Leaders need to be clear on what's healthy empathy and what is not.

pending_qa.q: What is emotional granularity and why is it critical for leadership effectiveness?
pending_qa.r: Emotional granularity is the ability to have a robust emotional lexicon and accurately name what you're experiencing. Research shows adults in this country can name and accurately identify only about three emotions—happy, sad, and pissed off—but there are about 85 to 90 emotions important for emotional granularity. This matters because the ability to access language that accurately reflects what we're feeling is crucial to the human experience. Emotional granularity ranked in the top five actionable skill sets for the future of leadership.

pending_qa.q: How does systems thinking and permeable boundaries relate to organizational resilience and AI investment success?
pending_qa.r: A healthy system requires permeable boundaries where good data and feedback can flow in and out freely. When boundaries close and feedback is not brought in consistently, organizations become self-referencing systems that believe they are great and know everything. MIT Sloan research shows 90% of AI investments fail with no return on investment, largely because of self-referencing systems. Leaders must have the courage to acknowledge that in times of disruption and emerging technology, they know very little.

pending_qa.q: What skill differentiates intelligent response from mere speed in leadership during times of disruption?
pending_qa.r: Leaders today must develop anticipatory awareness, temporal awareness, and situational awareness—the ability to read what they can't see, similar to a quarterback's pocket presence. This allows talented athletes and leaders to appear to slow down the game without actually creating more time. The distinction is between productivity urgency and strategic urgency, between risk-taking and strategic risk-taking. CEOs should focus on get strategic shit done (GSSD) rather than just getting shit done (GSD), because the current challenge is action over impact.
